title: System Explorer view documents
description: Operator-authored projections of the graph, served by the hub (docs/SPEC.md section 6.2). The envelope carries every document the configured directory holds, plus a per-document error entry for anything malformed — a broken view is an input to report, not a file to silently drop.

errors.description: Documents the directory holds that do not validate, each named with why. Present only when at least one is.

name.description: Stable identifier, kebab-case like every other key in the product.

hosts.description: Hub-registry host names this view was composed FOR; consumers offer it only there. Absent means every host — but a view is a dashboard composed for somewhere, so authored documents should usually name their hosts: the ZFS view rendering against a ZFS-less host as a wall of error strips is the shape this member exists to prevent. On a named host, panel failures still show loudly; targeting narrows where the view appears, never what it admits.

audience.description: Prose: who this projection is for. Documentation for the operator choosing a view, never machine-matched — audiences are people, not roles the product could pretend to enforce.

filters.description: Fact-equality filters, exactly the collection route's own (section 6): the panel IS a filtered collection, so it cannot express a question the API cannot.

columns.description: Fact NAMES, native spelling, in display order. Names only — meaning lives in /v1/facts and labels are the client's concern (section 5). A name no row carries renders empty, which is honest: the view said what to show, the host said what exists.

note.description: One optional sentence of operator prose under the panel title — what this panel is FOR, in the audience's words. The one place a view may speak, because it is the operator speaking, not the product.
